CVE-2025-11468.title: When folding a long comment in an email header containing exclusi ...
CVE-2025-11468.description: When folding a long comment in an email header containing exclusively unfoldable characters, the parenthesis would not be preserved. This could be used for injecting headers into email messages where addresses are user-controlled and not sanitized.

CVE-2025-12781.title: When passing data to the b64decode(), standard_b64decode(), and u ...
CVE-2025-12781.description:
When passing data to the b64decode(), standard_b64decode(), and urlsafe_b64decode() functions in the "base64" module the characters "+/" will always be accepted, regardless of the value of "altchars" parameter, typically used to establish an "alternative base64 alphabet" such as the URL safe alphabet. This behavior matches what is recommended in earlier base64 RFCs, but newer RFCs now recommend either dropping characters outside the specified base64 alphabet or raising an error. The old behavior has the possibility of causing data integrity issues.




This behavior can only be insecure if your application uses an alternate base64 alphabet (without "+/"). If your application does not use the "altchars" parameter or the urlsafe_b64decode() function, then your application does not use an alternative base64 alphabet.




The attached patches DOES NOT make the base64-decode behavior raise an error, as this would be a change in behavior and break existing programs. Instead, the patch deprecates the behavior which will be replaced with the newly recommended behavior in a future version of Python. Users are recommended to mitigate by verifying user-controlled inputs match the base64 
alphabet they are expecting or verify that their application would not be 
affected if the b64decode() functions accepted "+" or "/" outside of altchars.

CVE-2025-13462.title: The "tarfile" module would still apply normalization of AREGTYPE  ...
CVE-2025-13462.description: The "tarfile" module would still apply normalization of AREGTYPE (\x00) blocks to DIRTYPE, even while processing a multi-block member such as GNUTYPE_LONGNAME or GNUTYPE_LONGLINK. This could result in a crafted tar archive being misinterpreted by the tarfile module compared to other implementations.

CVE-2025-15282.title: User-controlled data URLs parsed by urllib.request.DataHandler al ...
CVE-2025-15282.description: User-controlled data URLs parsed by urllib.request.DataHandler allow injecting headers through newlines in the data URL mediatype.

CVE-2025-15366.description: The imaplib module, when passed a user-controlled command, can have additional commands injected using newlines. Mitigation rejects commands containing control characters.

CVE-2025-15367.title: The poplib module, when passed a user-controlled command, can hav ...
CVE-2025-15367.description:
The poplib module, when passed a user-controlled command, can have
additional commands injected using newlines. Mitigation rejects commands
containing control characters.

CVE-2026-0672.title: When using http.cookies.Morsel, user-controlled cookie values and ...
CVE-2026-0672.description: When using http.cookies.Morsel, user-controlled cookie values and parameters can allow injecting HTTP headers into messages. Patch rejects all control characters within cookie names, values, and parameters.

CVE-2026-103995.title: Response body and chunk parsing would handle non-hex or negative  ...
CVE-2026-103995.description: Response body and chunk parsing would handle non-hex or negative integers incorrectly which could result in misinterpreting HTTP response contents.

CVE-2026-114583.title: tarfile.tar_filter could be bypassed using crafted link entries,  ...
CVE-2026-114583.description:
tarfile.tar_filter could be bypassed using crafted link entries, including symlinks with empty or directory-like names, to redirect later archive members outside the intended extraction directory. This allowed a malicious tar archive to cause tarfile.extractall() with filter="tar" to write files outside the destination directory, subject to the permissions of the extracting process.

This is the tarfile.tar_filter counterpart of CVE-2026-7774, which covered tarfile.data_filter.

CVE-2026-115557.title: Python has added a denylist for known compromised certificates to ...
CVE-2026-115557.description: Python has added a denylist for known compromised certificates to the "ssl" module to ensure user safety even without certificate revocation configured. Known compromised certificates will automatically be rejected regardless of the SSLContext policy configuration.

CVE-2026-116566.title: socket.getaddrinfo() previously accepted null bytes within *host* ...
CVE-2026-116566.description: socket.getaddrinfo() previously accepted null bytes within *host* and *port* parameters which can cause the values to be silently truncated.

CVE-2026-11972.title: When using the "tarfile" module with a file opened in "streaming  ...
CVE-2026-11972.description: When using the "tarfile" module with a file opened in "streaming mode" (mode="r|") the tarfile module did not properly handle EOF, making archive parsing take exponentially longer.

CVE-2026-12345.title: The cleanup of tempfile.TemporaryDirectory is vulnerable to a rac ...
CVE-2026-12345.description: The cleanup of tempfile.TemporaryDirectory is vulnerable to a race condition. An attacker who can modify the tree during cleanup can replace a directory with a symbolic link, causing files outside of the temporary directory to be deleted or have their permissions and file flags reset, with the privileges of the process performing the cleanup. Note that platforms where shutil.rmtree.avoids_symlink_attacks is false, remain affected, and file flags may still be reset outside of the tree on all platforms.

CVE-2026-1299.title:
The 
email module, specifically the "BytesGenerator" class, didn’ ...
CVE-2026-1299.description:
The 
email module, specifically the "BytesGenerator" class, didn’t properly quote newlines for email headers when 
serializing an email message allowing for header injection when an email
 is serialized. This is only applicable if using "LiteralHeader" writing headers that don't respect email folding rules, the new behavior will reject the incorrectly folded headers in "BytesGenerator".

CVE-2026-19672.title:
The tarfile module's tar and data
 extraction filters created dir ...
CVE-2026-19672.description:
The tarfile module's tar and data
 extraction filters created directories outside the destination for 
members whose name leaves the destination and returns to it, such as ../evil/../dest/sub/file. The containment check used the resolved path, but intermediate directories were created from the name as given.

Only
 empty directories are created outside the destination. Member contents 
are still extracted inside it. To return to the destination the member's
 name must contain the destination directory's own final component, so 
extraction into a secure randomised directory is not affected.

This affects POSIX platforms only. On Windows, .. components are collapsed before the path reaches the filesystem, so the directories outside the destination are never created.

CVE-2026-3276.title: unicodedata.normalize() can take excessive CPU time when processi ...
CVE-2026-3276.description:
unicodedata.normalize() can take excessive CPU time when processing
specially crafted Unicode input containing long runs of combining characters
with alternating Canonical Combining Class values.
This affects all normalization forms.

CVE-2026-3446.title: When calling base64.b64decode() or related functions the decoding ...
CVE-2026-3446.description: When calling base64.b64decode() or related functions the decoding process would stop after encountering the first padded quad regardless of whether there was more information to be processed. This can lead to data being accepted which may be processed differently by other implementations. Use "validate=True" to enable stricter processing of base64 data.

CVE-2026-3479.title: DISPUTED: The project has clarified that the documentation was in ...
CVE-2026-3479.description:
DISPUTED: The project has clarified that the documentation was incorrect, and that pkgutil.get_data() has the same security model as open(). The documentation has been updated to clarify this point. There is no vulnerability in the function if following the intended security model.

pkgutil.get_data() did not validate the resource argument as documented, allowing path traversals.

CVE-2026-4360.title: In the Tarfile.extract() function, the filter parameter is not pa ...
CVE-2026-4360.description: In the Tarfile.extract() function, the filter parameter is not passed properly when extracting hardlinks. An affected system that extracts content from untrusted tar files could end up writing files with an unexpected uid/gid despite the user passing filter='data' to the extract() function.

CVE-2026-7210.title: `xml.parsers.expat` and `xml.etree.ElementTree` use insufficient  ...
CVE-2026-7210.description: `xml.parsers.expat` and `xml.etree.ElementTree` use insufficient entropy for Expat hash-flooding protection, which allows a crafted XML document to trigger hash flooding.\r\n\r\nFully mitigating this vulnerability requires both updating libexpat to 2.8.0 or later and applying this patch.

CVE-2026-115559.title: IMAP4.starttls() wraps the socket in TLS but leaves self._readbuf ...
CVE-2026-115559.description: IMAP4.starttls() wraps the socket in TLS but leaves self._readbuf, imaplib's own read-ahead buffer, untouched. Any plaintext bytes that arrived in the same recv() as the tagged OK to STARTTLS are returned by readline() after the handshake, so the client treats them as the first responses on the protected channel. A network attacker who cannot break TLS can append forged lines after the server's OK, let the handshake complete with the real server and a valid certificate, and have the client accept the forged CAPABILITY and the forged tagged completion of the next command. This is the STARTTLS command/response injection class of CVE-2011-0411.

CVE-2026-115791.title:
When tarfile or zipfile command line interface (CLI) is used to

 ...
CVE-2026-115791.description:
When tarfile or zipfile command line interface (CLI) is used to

decompress an archive, a Python script shadowing the stdlib can be

created. Then if an error occurs during decompressing the next file,

the newly created Python script is executed. This is especially true

if the created Python is called traceback.py. The problem is that

Python adds the current directory to sys.path when python -m MODULE is

run, and the archive is also decompressed in the current directory.



The fix removes sys.path[0] in gzip, tarfile and zipfile command line

interface to prevent shadowing standard library modules from extracted

files.

CVE-2026-119170.title: There was a regression in how FIPS algorithms were enforced for t ...
CVE-2026-119170.description: There was a regression in how FIPS algorithms were enforced for the hashlib module. Only users that are using OpenSSL in FIPS mode are affected. Only Python 3.14.10 is affected, all other Python versions are unaffected.

CVE-2026-124249.title: http.cookiejar.CookieJar deleted a stored cookie when a response  ...
CVE-2026-124249.description:
http.cookiejar.CookieJar deleted a stored cookie when a response carried an
already expired Set-Cookie header for it, using the Domain and Path
attributes from the header without consulting the cookie policy. A server
could therefore delete cookies belonging to other domains from a shared
cookie jar, such as the one used by urllib's HTTPCookieProcessor. The fix
consults the cookie policy before an expired cookie may delete an existing
one, as required by RFC 6265 section 5.3.

CVE-2026-19552.description: When ca_certs parameter was supplied to ssl.get_server_certificate() function, the identity of the certificate is not checked.
